events.description: 8. ** TEXT ONLY ORDER **The United States alleges that two Wisconsin towns have violated section 301 of the federal Help America Vote Act by failing to have at least one electronic voting system for use by disabled voters. The United States and the Town of Lawrence have negotiated a consent judgment, which the court is prepared to enter. However, the court will forestall action on the consent judgment until the State of Wisconsin has the opportunity to respond. The United States moves for a preliminary injunction against the Town of Thornapple. The court will hold an evidentiary hearing on the motion for injunction at 11:00 a.m., September 27, 2024. The Town of Thornapple has until September 25 to file any opposition. Any response to the proposed consent judgment or the motion for preliminary injunction from the State of Wisconsin must be filed by September 25. The United States may reply by September 26. Signed by District Judge James D. Peterson on 9/20/2024. (jls) (Entered: 09/20/2024)

events.description: 22. ** TEXT ONLY ORDER **The court held a preliminary injunction hearing at which it also heard oral argument on a motion to dismiss filed by the Town of Thornapple defendants, Dkt. 13 . For reasons stated at the hearing, the motion to dismiss, Dkt. 13, is DENIED; the United States' motion for a preliminary injunction against the Thornapple defendants, Dkt. 3, is GRANTED; and the joint motion by the United States and the Town of Lawrence defendants for entry of a partial consent judgment and order, Dkt. 2, is GRANTED. The United States and the Thornapple defendants have until the close of business on October 1, 2024, to submit to the court a proposed injunction; if they cannot agree to the terms, then the parties shall clearly and briefly identify their disagreements. This shall be a joint submission. The parties should also advise the court as to what they think should happen next to resolve this case in its entirety. The briefing schedule on the motion to dismiss is struck. Signed by District Judge James D. Peterson on 9/27/2024. (jls) (Entered: 09/27/2024)

events.description: 41. ** TEXT ONLY ORDER ** This court granted the government's motion for a preliminary injunction to require the Town of Thornapple and its employees to comply with the Help America Vote Act, 52 U.S.C. § 21081. Dkt. 22. The parties then agreed to the terms of the preliminary injunction, Dkt. 26, which the court approved, Dkt. 27 . Now the parties move to clarify "that the terms of the [preliminary injunction] that do not expressly reference the November 5, 2024, federal general election extend beyond that election." Dkt. 40 . The motion is GRANTED. Paragraphs (1), (4), and (5) are limited to the November 5 election, but the remaining provisions in the injunction are not so limited. Signed by District Judge James D. events.description: 51. ** TEXT ONLY ORDER ** The government contends that defendants are violating the Help America Votes Act by failing to provide a voting system that reasonably accommodates disabilities. This court issued a preliminary injunction, which the court of appeals affirmed. This court then directed the parties to identify the steps needed to resolve the case. Dkt. 48. In a joint submission, the parties say that they are in settlement talks, and they ask for 60 days to complete those talks. Dkt. 50 . The motion is GRANTED. The clerk of court is directed to set a scheduling conference before Magistrate Judge Boor in mid-December 2025. One week before the conference, the parties are to submit Rule 26(f) reports. If the parties notify the court of a settlement before then, the court will cancel the conference and strike the deadline for submitting reports. Signed by District Judge James D. Peterson on 09/26/2025. (acd) (Entered: 09/26/2025)

events.description: 56. ** TEXT ONLY ORDER ** In this case for enforcement of the Help America Vote Act, the federal government sued three sets of defendants: (1) the town of Lawrence and some of its officials; (2) the town of Thornapple and some of its officials; and (3) the state of Wisconsin. The court entered judgment against the Lawrence defendants in 2024. Dkt. 23 . The federal government has now settled its claims with the Thornapple defendants, Dkt. 53-1, and it moves to dismiss its claims against both the Thornapple defendants and the state with prejudice. Dkt. 55 . The motion is GRANTED, and those defendants are DISMISSED. This resolves all claims in the case, so the clerk of court is directed to close the case. Signed by District Judge James D. Peterson on 12/18/2025. (acd) (Entered: 12/19/2025)
